spans.s:
Śāṭyāyana, ‘descendant of Śāṭya,’ is the patronymic of a teacher mentioned twice in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa and often in the Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa. In a vaṃśa (list of teachers) in the latter work he is called a pupil of jvālāyana, while in the vaṃśa at the end of the Sāmavidhāna brāhmaṇa he appears as a pupil of bādarāyaṇa. The Śāṭyāyanins, his followers, are frequently mentioned in the Sūtras, the Śāṭyāyani brāhmaṇa and the Śāṭyāyanaka being also referred to in them. It has been shown by Oertel that this brāhmaṇa bore a close resemblance to, and probably belonged to the same period as, the Jaiminīya brāhmaṇa.
